Liu Bei said, “What blessing or curse does this omen mean?”

Zhuge Liang checked the stars in the sleeve and said, “Changsha has already been secured, and you will win another great general. After the Hour of the Horse it will be clear by daylight.”

Soon after, a small troop rider flew in and reported, “General Guan has already taken Changsha. He has accepted the surrender of Huang Zhong and Wei Yan. I request Your Majesty go to him at once.”

Liu Bei rejoiced and entered Changsha.

Guan Yu welcomed him into the main hall and relayed all about Huang Zhong. Liu Bei then visited Huang Zhong personally and invited him. Huang came out and surrendered. He asked that Han Xuan’s head be buried to the east of Changsha.

Later people composed this poem in praise of Huang Zhong:

The general’s spirit and bearing rose with Heaven and stars; his white hair still held him fast in the Han’s southern lands.
To die, he was content with no blame or reproach; even kneeling low before death, he still carried shame at the heart.
The treasured sword shone like bright snow and showed his divine courage; iron cavalry in the wind recalled the intoxication of war.
Across all ages his lofty name should never fade, forever following the lone moonlight over Xiangtan.

Liu Bei honored Huang Zhong greatly.

When Guan Yu brought Wei Yan before him, Zhuge Liang ordered the men with axes and blades to bring him out.

Liu Bei asked in alarm, “Wei Yan is a man with merit and without guilt. Why does the Military Adviser want him dead?”

Zhuge Liang replied, “To eat his salary and kill the ruler is disloyal. To live on one land and surrender that land is unrighteous. I see rebellion in Wei Yan’s mind. He will turn long afterward if left alive, so I cut him down now to cut off the root of future disaster.”

Liu Bei said, “If we kill him, all those who have surrendered will all feel their safety threatened. I ask the Military Adviser for clemency.”

Zhuge pointed at Wei Yan. “I spare your life now. Show that you can be loyal to the end and bear no strange thoughts. If such thoughts arise, I will in any case take your head.”

Wei Yan nodded repeatedly and withdrew.

Huang Zhong recommended Liu Biao’s nephew Liu Pan, who now sat in You County in idling seclusion.

Liu Bei brought him back and made him Administrator of Changsha Commandery.

With four commanderies already pacified, Liu Bei ended his campaign and returned to Jingzhou. He changed Youjiangkou into Gong’an.

From then on, money and grain flourished, worthy men came to join him, and commanders’ horses were distributed in dispersed camps across the mountain passes.

Now Zhou Yu returned to Chaisang to recuperate, and appointed Gan Ning to guard Baling Commandery and Ling Tong to hold Hanyang Commandery. At both places he positioned war junks, waiting for redeployment.

Cheng Pu brought his remaining officers and soldiers back to Hefei County.

Since the great battle after Red Cliffs, Sun Quan had long been at Hefei, clashing with Cao troops in more than ten engagements with no final victory. He had not dared to press hard against the city, keeping his army fifty li away.

When news came that Cheng Pu had arrived, Sun Quan rejoiced and personally came out to the camp to reward his soldiers.

Then it was reported that Lu Su had arrived first. Sun Quan dismounted and waited on the ground for him to approach, hastily dismounting and performing proper courtly greeting.

All the generals were astonished at Sun’s respect.

Sun asked Lu Su to mount up and rode beside him while holding the rein. He confided in him, “I came down from the saddle to receive you; does that show I do not honor you?”

Lu Su said, “No, my lord.”

Sun asked, “Then how else could I honor you?”

Lu Su replied, “May Your Majesty’s might and virtue extend over the four seas, bringing all nine provinces under one command, so that, after the empire is made, I may inscribe your illustrious name on bamboo and silk. Only then can you be truly glorious.”

Sun clapped his hands and laughed broadly, and together they went into the command tent for a full banquet, rewarding the weary soldiers who had fought in close fighting and discussing strategy to break the Hefei blockade.

Suddenly a messenger arrived: Zhang Liao had sent a challenge to battle.

Sun opened the letter and grew angry. “Zhang Liao has insulted me too far. You hear that Cheng Pu’s army has come; he has deliberately sent men to start a skirmish. Tomorrow I will not send fresh troops to meet them. I will fight one grand battle myself.”

He ordered that at the fifth watch that night all three armies leave camp and advance toward Hefei.

Around the hour of chen, when horse and men had gone halfway, Cao’s troops were already there; both sides had formed ranks.

Sun Quan dressed in gold helmet and gold armor and rode out. To his left rode Song Qian and to his right Jia Hua, both generals wielding fanged-tine halberds as escorts.

After three drumbeats, Cao’s lines opened their gate flags, and three fully armed generals in full armor mounted the front of their formation: Zhang Liao at the center, Li Dian on the left, and Yue Jin on the right.

Zhang Liao urged his horse forward and sought a determined contest with Sun himself.

Sun raised his spear as if to fight himself. A general with a raised spear and sudden mounted thrust came out into the center of the formation: it was Taishi Ci.

Zhang Liao swung his saber to meet him. The two commanders fought for seventy to eighty rounds, with no clear winner.

From among Cao’s ranks, Li Dian said to Yue Jin, “The man in the golden helmet is Sun Quan. If we capture him, we can answer a grievance for all eight hundred thirty thousand men.”

He had not finished saying this when Yue Jin rode in with one horse and one saber. He came on a diagonal path like a flash of lightning and in front of us.

He rose to strike with his blade. Song Qian and Jia Hua quickly used their halberds to block; both halberd shafts were cut in one stroke, and only the hafts struck toward the horse’s head.

Yue Jin wheeled around. Li Dian shot an arrow that struck Song Qian in the heart and dropped him from his horse.

Taishi Ci saw someone falling behind him, abandoned Zhang Liao, and turned back to his own ranks.

Seizing the moment, Zhang Liao charged forward and killed men through the ranks. Wu soldiers were thrown into confusion and scattered in all directions.

Zhang Liao saw Sun Quan and accelerated hard.

As he closed in, an army burst forward in the direction of the line, with General Cheng Pu in its lead. He intercepted and cut a passage, saving Sun.

Zhang Liao drew back his men and returned to Hefei.

Cheng Pu kept Sun safely in the great camp while the broken troops drifted back by themselves.

Seeing Song Qian dead, Sun Quan wept openly.

Zhang Hong said, “My lord relies on his robust strength and has been haughty toward a mighty foe. The whole of the three armies feels chilled in spirit. Even if one who cuts down generals and seizes banners can make one’s name shake the battlefield, this is still the duty of a lesser commander, not of the lord himself. Keep Your Majesty’s ferocity in check, and hold fast to plans for kingship and conquest.”

Sun said, “The fault is mine. From now on I will amend it.”

Soon afterward, Taishi Ci entered the tent and said, “One of my men is surname Ge, name Ding. He and a fellow man named the stablehand were former horse-stable mates under Zhang Liao.

the stablehand bore a grudge after being held back in rank. Tonight I have sent men to report by signal fire. He has come to Hefei city to ask to avenge Song Qian by killing Zhang Liao. I ask leave to send troops for an external operation.”

Sun said, “Where is this Ge Ding?”

Taishi Ci replied, “He has already slipped into Hefei city.”

He asked, “Allow me five thousand men.”

Zhuge Jin said, “Zhang Liao is deeply crafty. He may have arranged this in advance; we cannot act rashly.”

Taishi Ci pressed for action. Because Sun was wounded in heart by Song Qian’s death and eager to take revenge, he approved and gave five thousand men to Taishi Ci for the sortie.

Now Ge Ding was from Taishi Ci’s own home district.

That day he had mingled with the army and entered Hefei city with it. Soon he found the old stableman and they spoke together.

Ge Ding said, “I have already sent a message to General Taishi Ci. Tonight they must come to support me. How do you propose we proceed?”

The stableman replied, “This place is far from the main army at night. He cannot enter quickly. At most you should light a torch on the hay heap there, cry out revolt in front, and throw the city into disorder, then stab Zhang Liao from inside while the rest of the troops can break out as well.”

Ge Ding answered, “That plan is excellent.”

That night Zhang Liao returned from victory and rewarded the whole army. He ordered nobody to remove their armor and sleep in armor.

The officers said, “Today we won entirely. Wu troops have fled far. Why does the general not remove armor and rest?”

Zhang Liao said, “No. For a commander, let him not make joy of victory and despair of defeat. If Wu soldiers cross our line while unready and strike into emptiness, how could we meet it? Tonight’s guard must be even more vigilant than any previous night.”

Before his sentence ended, fire rose in the rear camp with a broad cry that looked and sounded like open revolt. Zhang Liao dismounted from his tent and called several dozen trusted officers and ministers to stand in front.

His men asked, “The calls are so urgent. Should we go look?”

Li Liao replied, “Can a whole city be in mutiny at once? This is a rebel man meant to panic the soldiers. When there is chaos first cut down the traitors.”

Not long after, Li Dian arrested Ge Ding and the stableman and brought them in.

After hearing the details, Zhang Liao had them executed at once before the horse.

Then from outside the city gate came gongs and war drums, and a great shout thundered.

Zhang Liao said, “That is likely the Wu force coming from outside. We can answer it. Bring a fire up inside the gate, let all shout mutiny, and open the gate wide. Lower the hanging bridge.”

Taishi Ci saw the gate gaping open and believed there was a revolt within, so he thrust his spear and rode in first.

From the wall, one cannon fired and arrows came down in a storm. Taishi Ci withdrew quickly and was hit by several arrows.

Behind him Li Dian and Yue Jin burst out. Wu soldiers lost more than half their force in that clash, and they pressed hard to the edge of the camp.

Lu Xun and Dong Xi broke out and saved Taishi Ci. Cao’s soldiers returned home.

Sun Quan saw Taishi Ci with grave wounds and grieved all the more.

Zhang Zhao asked him to end the campaign. Sun agreed and drew back, withdrawing the army onto ships and returning to Nanxu and Runzhou.

By the time the troops were quartered, Taishi Ci was in danger of death.

Sun sent Zhang Zhao and others to pay him visits.

Taishi Ci shouted, “A true man should be born in upheaval, carrying a three-foot sword, to achieve undying merit. What I meant to do has not yet been fulfilled. How then can I die?”

After he spoke, he died at forty-one years of age.

Later people praised him in verse:

Dedicated in loyalty and filial piety, Taishi Ci of the East.
His name would be known in distant lands, and his bow and horse rattled the roaring army.
The North Sea repaid his grace one day, and in Shen Pavilion he fought in battle intoxication.
At the end he spoke of noble resolve; all ages will sorrow with him.

When Sun Quan heard of Taishi Ci’s death, his sorrow did not cease. He ordered a rich burial at Nanxu, beneath Mount Beigu, and raised Taishi Xiang, his son, in the household.

Now Liu Bei was reorganizing soldiers and horses in Jingzhou. Hearing that Wu had been beaten at Hefei and returned to Nanxu, he discussed it with Zhuge Liang.

Zhuge Liang said, “Kongming observed the stars at night. He saw a star fall in the northwest. It means a member of the royal house will surely be broken.”

As he spoke, a messenger arrived to report Prince Liu Qi’s death.

Liu Bei wept bitterly and without end.

Zhuge Liang advised, “Life and death are fixed in Heaven. My lord must not worry and harm his health. Urgently send men to guard the city and to arrange the funeral rites.”

Liu Bei said, “Who can go?”

Zhuge Liang replied, “No one except Guan Yu can go.”

At once he ordered Guan Yu to go ahead and secure Xiangyang.

Liu Bei said, “Today Liu Qi is dead. East Wu will certainly come to attack Jingzhou. How shall we answer?”

Zhuge Liang said, “Should anyone come, I shall have a reply.”

Half a month passed. Men reported that Lu Su and others from Eastern Wu had arrived to offer condolences for the dead.

It was then that:

The plans and stratagems have already been laid and arranged; only the mission from Eastern Wu remains to arrive.
Who can say how Kongming will answer?

How this turned out will be told in the next chapter.
chapters.title: Guan Yunchang Righteously Releases Huang Hansheng; Sun Zhongmou Battles Zhang Wenyuan

chapters.html:
When Zhuge Liang, whose courtesy name was Kongming, heard that Lu Su had arrived, he and Liu Bei, whose courtesy name was Xuande, went out of the city to receive him. They brought him to the public office; after they had met and exchanged formal words, Lu Su spoke first.

“Your lord heard of the death of his nephew and, in mourning, made a modest offering, sending me to present it. Chief Commander Zhou, whose courtesy name was Gongjin, has conveyed repeated greetings to Imperial Uncle Liu and Master Zhuge.”

Liu Bei and Kongming rose and thanked him. They accepted the gifts, and he was invited to drink.

Lu Su said, “Formerly, the Imperial Uncle spoke this way: ‘If the master is absent, Jing Province should be returned at once.’ Now that the master has died, he will surely return. When, then, can we finalize the handover?”

Liu Bei replied, “Drink first, Master Lu. There is a matter I would discuss.”

Lu Su drank several cups at Kongming’s insistence, then resumed.

Before Liu Bei could answer, Kongming’s face changed.

“Zijing, it is no use to talk in circles; one should wait until one is asked to speak. Since my former High Emperor launched a rebellion by ‘slaying the snake,’ established a base and founding charge, and passed the mantle down to this day, evil tyrants have arisen together, each seized a region, and Heaven’s way has now turned the whole back toward the true succession. My lord is descended from King Jing of Zhongshan and is Emperor Xiaojing’s great-grandson by lineage. He is the Son of Heaven’s uncle now; how could not he be allowed to divide and reclaim by right? Liu Jingsheng was my lord’s elder brother. A younger brother follows the elder’s task; what rule of conduct is violated?

“Your lord, born a mere petty clerk of Qiantang, has done nothing of merit in court. Yet with coercive force he now holds six commanderies and eighty-one provinces, and still his greed is not sated, while he seeks to swallow Han territory. The realm belongs to the house of Liu, and if my lord bears that surname, he should not be denied a share; yet your lord, surnamed Sun, still dares to contend for it.

“At Red Cliffs, my lord bore heavy toil and risk, and all his commanders obeyed him. Surely our return was not only your Eastern Wu alone. If I had not borrowed the southeastern wind, could Brother Zhou have shown even half his stratagem?

“One victory in Jiangnan—leave aside the two Qiaos being in the Copper-Sparrow Palace—would still mean that even your house and children could not be saved.

“Yet now, when my lord did not at once answer, I thought Zijing to be a man of clear understanding, and I had thought no further explanation needed. Why do you still fail to see how grave this is?”

Lu Su closed his mouth with no reply. After a while, he said, “Master Kongming may indeed be right in reasoning. I suffer only this: how can I reply for myself in person?”

Kongming said, “What is so unbearable?”

Lu Su replied, “When Emperor-uncle was in peril at Dangyang, it was I who brought Master Kongming across the river and presented him to my lord. Later, when Chief Commander Zhou sought to raise troops to take Jing Province, it was again I who held him off. Since he first said, ‘After the lordship is gone, return Jing Province,’ it was again I who bore that burden. Now I cannot keep to my earlier words. How can I return with a proper answer? My lord and Chief Commander Zhou will surely be at fault. Lu Su does not resent dying, but only fears stirring up war against Eastern Wu and leaving Liu Bei unable to sit peacefully in Jing Province, a mere object of humiliation.”

Kongming said, “Cao Cao commands a million under the name of the Son of Heaven, but that does not move me. Why should one fear a mere child, a Lord Zhou?”

“If it worries Master Lu’s face in this audience, then I urge my lord to draft a paper document: let us temporarily borrow Jing Province as a base. When my lord finds other cities, he will hand it back to Eastern Wu. Is that not sound?”

Lu Su asked, “To what place will your lord return what you borrow?”

Kongming answered, “The Central Plains are not yet ready for us to seize. In the West of Sichuan, Liu Zhang is dim and weak. My lord intends to take it. If he takes West Sichuan, then he will return what is owed.”

Lu Su, helpless, consented.

Liu Bei wrote a document with his own hand and sealed it. Master Zhuge Liang also sealed it. Kongming said, “If the Imperial Uncle is a man of his own part, he cannot stand surety for himself alone. Please, Zijing, place your seal too, that it looks proper when you report it to the Wu lord.”

Lu Su bowed and did so.

After the banquet they took leave. Liu Bei and Kongming sent him to the riverside. Kongming instructed, “Zijing, when you return to Wu lord, speak to him in full and with good feeling. Do not let him forget this in the future. If he rejects our document, I will change my face and seize eighty-one provinces as well. All we need now is peace between the two houses. Do not give the Wei bandits anything to laugh at.”

Lu Su departed by boat and returned first to Chaisang Commandery to see Zhou Yu. The Chief Commander asked, “How did this negotiation for Jing Province proceed?”

Lu Su said, “I have the document here,” and presented it.

Zhou Yu kicked the ground hard. “You have been taken in by Master Zhuge’s plot! In name, this is a loan; in truth, a cunning cheat. He says he will return it only after he takes West Sichuan. Tell me: do you know when he can take it? If ten years pass and he has not taken West Sichuan, then ten years and no return? What use is this piece of writing, and yet you served as guarantor! If he does not return, you will be dragged in, too. How can my lord answer for this?”

On hearing these words, Lu Su stood silent a while and said, “I fear Liu Bei will not betray me.”

Zhou Yu said, “You are an honest man, Zijing. Liu Bei is a predator; Zhuge Liang is a slippery schemer. They may not be what your heart assumes.”

Lu Su asked, “If this is true, what then?”

Zhou Yu answered, “You are my benefactor—do you forget how you once showed me mutual kindness, sharing wine? How should I not return it to save you? Stay here for a few days and keep calm. When reports arrive from Jiangbei, I will make other arrangements.”

Lu Su remained restless and restless.

After several days, a spy reported: “Inside Jing Province, mourning banners are raised in the city; new mounds are being built outside the walls, and soldiers hang their mourning attire.”

Zhou Yu asked sharply, “Who has died?”

The spy answered, “Lord Liu Bei’s consort, Lady Gan, has died, and the funeral is being arranged at once.”

Zhou Yu said to Lu Su, “My plan is complete. If we get Liu Bei to submit and be confined, Jing Province can be taken in a moment.”

Lu Su asked, “Then how do we set it in motion?”

Zhou Yu replied, “Liu Bei has lost his wife and must soon remarry. I have a sister of unusual strength and courage; she commands hundreds of maidservants and keeps them ready with blades. Their armories fill her halls and yards. A woman, she is no weaker than a man.

“I will write to the lord at once and send a matchmaker to Jing Province saying that Liu Bei is to enter as a son-in-law by marriage transfer. Once he is brought south to Jiangxu, if we cannot tie him by a bride, he may be quietly confined in prison, and men can be dispatched to fetch Jing Province in exchange for Liu Bei. When the city walls are handed over, I will have another design. See that nothing stains your own person.”

Lu Su thanked him.

Zhou Yu wrote the letter and placed it before him. As soon as Lu Su was on his way south, he presented it to Chief Commander Sun Quan. The king read it and frowned.

“You have such poor judgment! A document like this—what use will it serve?”

Lu Su answered, “Chief Commander Zhou has enclosed a letter and a plan. It could win us Jing Province.”

Sun Quan read it and, though he nodded inwardly in approval, thought hard, “Who can go?” Then a sudden realization came: “Only Lu Fan can do it.” He summoned Lu Fan at once.

Sun Quan said, “I have just heard Liu Bei has lost his consort. I have a sister and wish to take him in marriage, binding our two houses forever so that together we can shatter Cao and uphold the Han court. No one but Ziheng can stand as matchmaker. Go at once to Jing Province and speak plainly.”

Lu Fan took command. That same day he prepared boats, took a few attendants, and headed for Jing Province.

In Jing Province, after Liu Bei had lost Lady Gan, grief sat with him by day and by night. One day, as he spoke quietly with Kongming, an attendant announced that a messenger from Eastern Wu had arrived: Lu Fan.

Kongming smiled. “This is Zhou Yu’s plan, clearly for Jing Province. I myself will remain behind a screen and listen in. Whatever he says, my lord should assent. Send him to the guesthouse first and give him rest; then we will discuss further in private.”

Liu Bei invited Lu Fan with formality. After courtesy was rendered, they sat.

After tea, Liu Bei asked, “If Ziheng has come, he surely bears some message?”

Lu Fan said, “I was told the Imperial Uncle lacked a husband and so there is a good match, and I came without hesitation to act as matchmaker, for fear this was no suitable chance to avoid. I do not know your will.”

Liu Bei answered, “In middle age a wife’s loss is bitter indeed. Her bones are still not cold; how can one speak of marriage now?”

Lu Fan said, “A man without a wife is like a house without a beam—how can he leave the order of humanity halfway and discard it? My lord Wu has a sister who is beautiful and virtuous and able to serve with tireless devotion. If these two houses conclude a bond as strong as old Qin and Jin did, the Wei rebels will not dare look south in confidence. This would profit both family and state. I beg your Lordship not to doubt it. Yet our Great Lady of Wu loves the child and refuses to send her far away; she insists only that Liu Bei come to Wu to wed.”

Liu Bei said, “Is the king aware?”

Lu Fan said, “How could I dare arrive before giving first report to my lord?”

Liu Bei said, “I am near fifty, and my hair is now graying. Your lord’s sister is of prime youth. I fear we are unmatched in age.”

Lu Fan said, “Though she is a woman, Lady Wu is bolder than men. She says, ‘Unless a man is a hero of the realm, I will not take him as husband.’ Your fame now spans the four seas; she is no different from saying this is precisely a lady for a worthy husband and a worthy husband for a lady. Why should age alone offend?”

Liu Bei said, “Go no farther tonight. I will send word in the morning.”

They entertained Lu Fan that day. At evening, Liu Bei and Kongming consulted.

Kongming said, “I already understand their purpose. I just checked the I Ching, and the omen is one of great favor.”

“The lord can agree. First send Sun Qian and Lu Fan back to Wu lord. Let him accept this as settled and choose a day to join them.”

Liu Bei said, “Chief Commander Zhou devised this scheme to harm Liu Bei. Is it safe for me to enter a place so dangerous on so light a wager?”

Kongming laughed aloud. “Though Zhou Yu can scheme, can he truly act beyond what Zhuge Liang can account for? A small ruse is enough. We can prevent Zhou Yu from opening his own stratagem fully. Besides, this is Wu lord’s sister, and the matter is now tied to my lord’s person. Jingzhou will not be lost.”

Liu Bei remained unconvinced.

Kongming then sent Sun Qian south with the marriage details. Sun Qian took the words and, with Lu Fan, arrived in Wu to report to Sun Quan.

Sun Quan said, “I, too, wish to take my younger sister as Liu Bei’s bride. I bear no other motive.”

Sun Qian bowed in thanks and returned to Jing Province, reporting the lord’s openness to the alliance.

Liu Bei still hesitated to go. Kongming said, “I have set three tactics in order, and only Zilong can carry them out.” He called Zhao Yun to him, whispered in his ear, and said, “Guard my lord when he goes to Wu. You are to carry these three silk pouches. Each contains a stratagem. Use them in order.”

He tucked the three pouches against Zhao Yun’s side and sent another emissary to secure the formal betrothal in Eastern Wu. All was arranged.

It was the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Jian’an. Liu Bei, Zhao Yun, and Sun Qian took ten fast boats with over five hundred men and departed Jing Province for Nanxu. All matters in Jing Province were left to Kongming’s judgment.

Liu Bei, though, was uneasy in his heart. When they came to Jiangnan, the boats lay at the bank. Zhao Yun said, “The Strategist entrusted me with three pouches of excellent counters. Since we have arrived, we should open the first now.”

They opened the first pouch and followed its instructions as given. The five hundred soldiers were each ordered to do as commanded. When their tasks were done, the troops moved out. He instructed Liu Bei to go first to visit Master Qiao.

The one called Qiao Gu-Lao, father of the two Qiaos, lived in Nanxu. Liu Bei led a mule carrying wine and went first to make his visit, explaining that Lu Fan was acting as matchmaker and that he had come to take a bride.

The five hundred following soldiers, dressed in red and with festive ribbons, went into the southern city to buy gifts and goods. In every street they announced that Liu Bei had entered Wu as a son-in-law. Sun Quan, hearing that Liu Bei had arrived, ordered Lu Fan to host him and give lodging in the guesthouses.

When Qiao Gu-Lao saw Liu Bei, he carried him to meet Lady Wu and offered congratulations. She asked, “What is this happy matter?”

“Lady, you had promised my daughter-in-law to Liu Bei,” Qiao said. “Liu Bei has now arrived. Why keep it hidden?”

Lady Wu gasped and said, “I know nothing of this, sir.” She sent someone to the lord for confirmation, and at once another to investigate in the city.

The reports all returned, “It is true. The son-in-law has already arrived and rests at the guesthouse. Five hundred men who came with him are shopping in the city for pork, sheep, fruit, and ceremonial supplies for the wedding. The matchmaker is Lu Fan, and Sun Qian acts for the groom’s side; both remain in the guesthouse.”

Lady Wu was startled.

After a short while, Sun Quan entered the rear hall to see his mother. She struck her chest and wept loudly.

“Mother, why are you troubled so deeply?” Sun Quan asked.

She replied, “Have you treated me as a mere stone? At the hour of peril, what instruction did my sister leave you?”

Sun Quan, startled, asked, “Mother, speak plainly. Why this sorrow?”

Mother said, “A man should marry when he is a man; a woman should marry when she is a woman. It is the way of all ages. I am your mother and may command the household. You bring Liu Bei as a son-in-law without telling me? My daughter is my daughter!”

Sun Quan asked in alarm, “How did this message reach you?”

She answered, “If you wished to hide it, perhaps only a fool could not know. In this city every commoner knows. You have concealed this from me.”

Qiao Gu-Lao said, “Elderly man here has known it many days and came only now to offer congratulations.”

Sun Quan said, “No, this is Zhou Yu’s plan. To take Jing Province he has used this as the pretext and lured Liu Bei into confinement, forcing him to exchange the city. If he refuses, he intends to execute him first. This is strategy, not sincere intent.”

Lady Wu shouted in anger at Zhou Yu.

“You, Gongjin, called general of six commanderies and eighty-one provinces, without one proper strategy for taking Jing Province, have made my daughter a lure of beautiful charm! If Liu Bei is killed, she becomes a widow before seeing the gate, and what then is left of this marriage for later? You have ruined one generation of my daughter’s life! You all are masters of display!”

Qiao Gu-Lao added, “If this plan succeeds, even if Jing Province is gained, the world will mock us. This cannot stand.”

His words left Sun Quan silent.

Lady Wu did not cease cursing Zhou Yu. Qiao Gu-Lao urged, “This has gone this far. Liu Imperial Uncle is kin to the Han house. Better to receive him as a true son-in-law and avoid open shame.”

Sun Quan said, “I fear the ages may not match.”

Qiao Gu-Lao replied, “Liu Imperial Uncle is one of this age’s great figures. If you make him your son-in-law, your sister will never be disgraced.”

Lady Wu said, “I have never met this Liu Imperial Uncle. At dawn I am to meet him at Ganlu Temple. If he is not to my liking, do as you wish; if he is, I will marry my daughter myself.”

Sun Quan was filial and, hearing such from his mother, immediately assented. He called Lu Fan outside.

“Tell Jia Hua’s detachment to bring three hundred halberd-men and hide beneath both colonnades. If Lady Wu refuses, one shout and one blast from all sides, and take him down.”

He told Lu Fan then to prepare accordingly and wait for the mother’s motion.

Later Qiao Gu-Lao took leave of Lady Wu and sent word to Liu Bei: “Tomorrow, at Ganlu Temple, my lord’s mother personally wishes to see him. Handle yourself carefully.”

Liu Bei and Sun Qian and Zhao Yun discussed. Zhao Yun said, “Tomorrow’s meeting has more peril than joy. I will bring the five hundred out as guard.”

The next day Lady Wu and Qiao Gu-Lao were seated first in the abbot’s hall of Ganlu Temple. Sun Quan arrived with a group of strategists and then ordered Lu Fan to summon Liu Bei from the guesthouse.

Liu Bei came wearing light armor under brocade robes, with attendants close at his side bearing his sword, and mounted. The men had all already arrived. He dismounted at the gate and entered.

Zhao Yun came fully armed with sidearm and all fittings, and a full band of five hundred marched behind him. At the temple gate they dismounted. Liu Bei first saw Sun Quan. The ruler’s eyes held concern as he took measure of Liu Bei’s bearing.

After both had exchanged formal courtesy, they entered the abbot’s hall and then went to present themselves to Lady Wu.

When Lady Wu saw Liu Bei she rejoiced and said to Qiao Gu-Lao, “He is truly a son-in-law fit for me.”

Qiao Gu-Lao said, “His posture is like a dragon and phoenix, handsome as Heaven’s sun and day itself. His virtue spreads across the world. Lady Wu, you are truly fortunate to gain such a groom.”

Liu Bei bowed and gave thanks. They dined together in the hall.

After a while, Zilong entered with sword drawn and took his place beside Liu Bei.

Lady Wu asked, “Who is this man?”

Liu Bei answered, “He is Zhao Zilong of Changshan.”

Lady Wu said, “Is he not the one who carried Ah Dou at the Long Slope at Dangyang?”

“Indeed,” Liu Bei said.

Lady Wu said, “A true general indeed.” She then offered him wine.

Zhao Yun whispered to Liu Bei, “I just inspected the corridor and saw halberd-men concealed there. There is no good intent. Tell Lady Wu of this.”

Liu Bei knelt before her seat and wept. “If one were to kill Liu Bei, I request that death be decreed at once.”

Lady Wu asked sharply, “Why say so?”

He answered, “From the corridor below I saw concealed halberd-men. If not to kill me, then for what purpose?”

Lady Wu grew furious and reproached Sun Quan, “Now that Liu Bei is already my son-in-law, he is my child by marriage as well. How dare you station halberd-men in this corridor?”

Sun Quan pretended ignorance and called Lu Fan for explanation. Lu Fan pointed at Jia Hua. Lady Wu called Jia Hua to account; he did not answer.

She ordered, “Cut him down!”

Liu Bei said, “If you execute a great general, it is not good for kinship. I am unlikely to remain seated at your hearth long.”

Qiao Gu-Lao also interceded. Lady Wu then shouted Jia Hua away. The halberd-men all withdrew in fear, heads lowered.

Liu Bei changed his robe and left the hall. In the yard he noticed a stone slab. He took the sword from his attendant, raised it to heaven, and swore: “If I can return to Jing Province and complete my kingly work, one stroke of this sword shall split this rock in two. If I die here, then though I hack at it this sword shall not open it.”

He raised his hand and struck. Sparks burst and the stone split in two.

From behind, Sun Quan had watched and asked, “Why does Liu Bei bear such resentment against the stone?”

Liu Bei said, “At fifty years I have not quelled bandits for the realm. I have long blamed myself. Yet this is my fortunate meeting—to be invited by Lady Wu as son-in-law. When I prayed at dawn for heaven, I asked for a sign: if I break Cao and revive Han, then this rock should be cleft. It has now happened.”

Sun Quan thought silently, “Could Liu Bei be speaking to mislead me?” and drew his own sword. He declared, “I too sought an omen from heaven. If I break the Wei traitors, I too shall split this stone.”

He drew and cut with full force. The rock, too, cracked.

To this day the split cross-grain mark is still seen.

Later generations wrote this verse:

The jeweled blade fell and split the mountain stone; where the golden ring rang, fire flared in the air. Fortune for both dynasties followed the decree of heaven; from this moment, heaven and earth stood on trifold balance.

The two men sheathed their swords and returned together to the hall. They drank several rounds. Sun Qian kept watch on Liu Bei.

Liu Bei then excused himself. “I do not bear the force of more wine,” he said. Sun Quan escorted him out to the temple gate. The two stood together and looked at the river and the hills.

Liu Bei said, “This is the finest terrain under heaven.”

It would later be written on the Ganlu Temple stele: “the first of all landscapes under heaven.”

Later generations composed:

Clear sky after rain, the riverland wraps the blue snails of green stone; Here is where once the heroes fixed their gaze, and the cliffs still resist storm and wave.

The two viewed these sights again and again. The wind grew fierce, stormy flood rose like whirling snow, and white waves reared upward. Suddenly a small boat, no larger than a leaf, moved across the river as though the surface were flat.

Liu Bei sighed, “‘Southern men steer ships; northern men ride horses’—so it is indeed true.”

Sun Quan inwardly thought, “Liu Bei says I have no habit of riding in the saddle, and this is not a sport I accept,” and ordered someone to bring a horse. He jumped on and drove down the mountain at a run, then up with lash and spur.

He laughed: “Can southern men not ride?”

Liu Bei pulled his robe and sprang to a horse with one leap, then shot down the slope and away and back up. The two men stopped at the hillside and, reins loose, laughed aloud.

To this day the place has been called “Zhuma Slope” (the Place of Stopped Horses).

Later generations composed:

Riding fast with charger’s heart and tiger-mare breath, the two men held their reins and watched the land and rivers; East Wu and West Shu alike become kings of the realm, and for ten thousand ages this slope remains.

The two returned side by side. The people of Nanxu rejoiced.

Liu Bei returned to the guesthouse and conferred with Sun Qian.

“Let us hasten to complete this marriage,” Sun Qian advised. “My lord should petition Qiao Gu-Lao soon and avoid further matters.”

The next day Liu Bei returned again and dismounted before Qiao Gu-Lao’s hall.

Qiao Gu-Lao received him and, after formalities and tea, Liu Bei said, “The men of Jiangzuo look for causes against me. I fear I cannot stay long.”

Qiao Gu-Lao replied, “Be of no fear. I have informed Lady Wu, and she has ordered protection.”

After a bow and blessing, Liu Bei returned. Qiao Gu-Lao entered to report that Liu Bei feared for his safety and wanted to return.

Lady Wu said in anger, “Who dares to harm my son-in-law?” She ordered him moved into the academy at once and said a date for marriage should be chosen.

Liu Bei spoke to her: “I fear Zilong’s distance outside with troops hard to keep in order.”

She ordered he be moved into her own residence instead of the guesthouse to prevent trouble. Liu Bei was quietly relieved.

Within a few days, a grand feast was arranged. Lady Sun married Liu Bei.

When the guests departed for the night, two rows of red torches guided Liu Bei into the bridal chamber. Beneath the lamp-light he saw spears and sabers packed all around; the maidservants all wore blades on their belts, stationed at both sides. His spirit seemed ready to leave his body.

Startled, he saw maidservants standing with crossed knives—he thought the men of Wu had set an ambush.

How this turned out will be told in the next chapter.
chapters.title: Lady Wu’s Temple Visit and Liu the Imperial Uncle’s Bridal Chamber

chapters.html:
Liu Bei stirs Lady Sun with craft; Zhuge Liang unleashes his second stratagem against Zhou Gongjin.

The narrative says Liu Bei saw that Lady Sun's room had spears and blades arranged along both sides, and all her attendants wore swords. He could not help but turn pale. A house stewardess stepped forward and said, "My lord, do not be alarmed. Lady Sun has loved watching martial displays since childhood and always told her attendants to fence with swords for recreation. This is why the room is so set."

Liu Bei said, "This is no matter for the lady to watch. My heart is unsettled. You should have it cleared for a time."

The house stewardess reported to Lady Sun, who said, "The weapons are all in the room, and the lady is uneasy as a lady guest is present. Now we can have them removed."

Lady Sun laughed. "After two lives in bloodshed, can you still fear weapons?" she said, then ordered them taken away and told the attendants to sheathe their swords and wait nearby.

That night Liu Bei and Lady Sun were joined as husband and wife, and they shared close joy for the long days. Liu Bei gave the attendants gold and silk to buy their goodwill, and had Sun Qian return first to Jing Province with the happy report. From then on, they drank together for days. Empress Dowager Sun favored her greatly.

Then Sun Quan sent a messenger to Zhou Yu in Chaisang Commandery: "My mother insisted on this and has already given my sister in marriage to Liu Bei. Who would have imagined that a feigned match would become true? How should we now proceed?"

On hearing this, Zhou Yu was greatly shocked; he could not sit or lie still. He formulated a plan, wrote a secret letter, and sent it back with the messenger for Sun Quan to read.

The letter read:

The scheme you planned has turned out not as expected. Since this has become real, we should now make use of it. Liu Bei is a man of tiger-like force, and he has General Guan, General Zhang, Zhao Yun, and Zhuge Liang with him. He is not one who bows easily for long. It would be best to soften him here in Wu, build grand houses and halls to dull his heart; send him abundant treasures and silks and beautiful gifts to please his eyes and ears. Then separate him from Guan, Zhang, and Zhao, and distance him from Zhuge Liang; place them in different locations. Then, when he is thus separated, strike him with troops and the matter will be secure. If you let him go now, he may be a dragon that has found rain; he is no mere creature of a pond. May the Lord consider this carefully."

Sun Quan read the letter and showed it to Zhang Zhao.

Zhang Zhao said, "Gongjin's plan matches my own thoughts exactly. Liu Bei rose from obscurity and ran all over the world; he has never enjoyed wealth or rank. If we now give him grand halls and courtyards, household attendants, and treasures of gold and jade, he will naturally drift away from Kongming, Guan, and Zhang. Then each will nurture resentment and Jing Province can be planned against. My lord, let you follow Gongjin's plan and carry it out quickly."

Sun Quan rejoiced and immediately had the East Mansion repaired, planted many trees and flowers, arranged every utensil in abundance, and invited Liu Bei and his sister to live there. He also added dozens of female musicians, along with gold, jade, and brocade toys and objects. Empress Dowager Sun thought this was only Sun Quan's kindness and rejoiced without measure.

Indeed Liu Bei became absorbed in music and beauty and did not think to return to Jing Province.

Now Zhao Yun with five hundred troops stayed before the East Mansion and had no duties, only riding out beyond the walls to shoot arrows and run horses. When the year came to its end, he reflected: "Kongming gave me three brocade pouches and said this: when I arrived in Nánxú, open the first; after I stayed through the year-end, open the second; when danger leaves no path, open the third. Each contains his divine stratagem. They all kept my lord alive and saved him once. This is now near year-end. My lord is enthralled by women and does not come out. Why not open the second pouch and act on it?"

So he opened it and read. It was indeed a marvelous stratagem. He went straight to the hall to see Liu Bei.

An attendant announced, "Zi'long has urgent matter for my lord."

Liu Bei called him in and asked what had occurred.

Zhao Yun feigned surprise and alarm and said, "Your lordship rests in painted halls and does not think of Jing Province, is this so?"

Liu Bei asked, "What is this that has startled us so?"

Zhao Yun said, "Early this morning Kongming sent word by messenger that Cao Cao seeks to repay the feud of the battle at Red Cliffs. He has raised five hundred thousand elite troops and marched all the way toward Jing Province. It is most grave. Your lord should return at once."

Liu Bei said, "I must discuss this with my wife."

Zhao Yun replied, "If you ask permission, surely she will not let you return. Better to tell her nothing and begin the march tonight. Delay will cost us."

Liu Bei said, "Withdraw for now. I will reason this out."

Zhao Yun deliberately pressed him several times and then left. Liu Bei entered Lady Sun's apartment, tears falling in secret.

Lady Sun said, "Husband, why this grief?"

Liu Bei said, "I think of my own person drifting in foreign lands. I cannot attend my parents, nor can I offer sacrifice to our ancestors. I have become gravely unfilial. Now, when the new year is near, the thought chokes me."

Lady Sun said, "Do not hide it from me. I have already learned it. A moment ago Zi'long reported that Jing Province is in grave peril and you wanted to return; he said this in order to leave."

Liu Bei knelt and said, "Since you already know, how could I still hide? If I stay, Jing Province may fall and I will be mocked by men; if I go, I cannot leave you. It is for this reason that I am troubled."

Lady Sun said, "I have served my lord, and wherever you go, my lord can lead. I will go with you."

Liu Bei said, "Lady, though your heart is generous, what of Empress Dowager and the Prince? Will they consent to this? If Lady pitying Liu Bei asks it, you might leave after a temporary farewell."

After tears poured down like rain and he finished speaking, Lady Sun said, "Husband, do not be troubled. I will make my mother a painful plea and force her to send me with you."

Liu Bei said, "Even if Empress Dowager permits it, Wu Hou will still oppose us."

After Lady Sun thought long in silence, she said, "The day we paid respect at first dawn, we can claim that we go to the river to offer sacrifice to our ancestors. We need not inform anyone and can leave that way."

Liu Bei knelt in gratitude and said, "If you do this, I could never forget it even in life and death. Do not let this leak out."

The matter was decided in private. Liu Bei quietly summoned Zhao Yun and gave him instructions: "On the first day of the new year, you should lead the troops out first and wait along the highway. I will say I am coming to make the ancestral offering and go with my wife."

Zhao Yun took his leave.

In the spring of the fifteenth year of Jian'an, on the first day of the first month, Wu Hou gathered civil and military officials in the hall. Liu Bei and Lady Sun paid their respects to Empress Dowager Sun.

Lady Sun said, "My husband long to honor his parents and ancestral tombs. They all rest in Zhuo Commandery, and he grieves day and night. Today he wishes to go to the riverbank and look northward to sacrifice. I can only tell my mother this."

Empress Dowager said, "This is filial piety. Who could deny it? Though you do not know an aunt by marriage, you may accompany your husband. It is fitting for a wife."

Lady Sun together with Liu Bei bowed and took leave.

At this time, only Sun Quan was in ignorance.

Lady Sun climbed into the carriage with only a few personal soft goods. Liu Bei mounted his horse and led several riders out of the city, where he met Zhao Yun. With five hundred soldiers clearing ahead and behind to protect, he left Nánxú behind and hurried on.

That night Sun Quan was drunk, and attendants guided him into the back hall. All civil and military officials were gone. By the time the officers learned Liu Bei and his wife had fled, night had deepened. They tried to report it to Sun Quan, but he had not sobered.

When he fell asleep, it was already the fifth watch.

Next day Sun Quan learned they had fled. He quickly summoned civil and military officers to meet and asked Zhang Zhao: "This man left us today; he will certainly cause chaos at night and day. We should pursue at once."

Sun Quan ordered Chen Wu and Pan Zhang to choose five hundred picked soldiers and chase without pause and bring them back. The two commanders took command and rode out.

Sun Quan's resentment against Liu Bei was so deep that he shattered the ink slab on the desk.

Cheng Pu said, "My lord has rage reaching the sky. I think Chen Wu and Pan Zhang will not catch this man."

Sun Quan said, "How dare I disobey my lord?"

Pu replied, "the Commandery Princess, Lady Sun has loved martial spectacles since youth and is firm and severe. All commanders fear her. Now that she chose to follow Liu Bei, she will stand loyal. If we chase the one she has gone with, how can we take him when she is there?"

Sun Quan became furious. He drew the sword he carried and called Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai: "You two take this sword. Capture my sister and bring me Liu Bei's head. Whoever disobeys, I will execute at once!"

Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai took the order and soon after led three thousand soldiers in pursuit.

Liu Bei whipped up the reins and rode hard; they only rested for two watches in the night before rising again in haste. Soon they reached the border of Chaisang. In the distance they saw a great cloud of dust behind. A messenger shouted: "The pursuers have arrived!"

Liu Bei asked in alarm, "Now that pursuit has come, what are we to do?"

Zhao Yun said, "My lord should press forward. I will hold behind for now."

When they reached the slope before the mountain, a troop surged forth and blocked the road. In front were two senior commanders who shouted hoarsely, "Liu Bei, dismount and submit. I hold the order of Chief Commander Zhou and have waited here a long time!"

In truth, Zhou Yu, fearing Liu Bei might get away, had first sent Xu Sheng and Ding Feng with three thousand horse and infantry to camp at a key chokepoint and have men watch from high points. He had counted on Liu Bei passing this route. On the day he saw their approach, he ordered them to draw weapons and block the way.

Liu Bei, alarmed, drew back his horse and asked Zhao Yun: "There is a blockade ahead and pursuit behind. With no road before or behind, what are we to do?"

Zhao Yun said, "Do not be alarmed. The strategist has three excellent plans, most of which are in the brocade pouches. We opened two and both proved true. The third remains unopened and may be opened only in desperate times. Yet this is desperate. We should open it now."

He opened it and handed it to Liu Bei.

Liu Bei read and came quickly to the front to Liu Bei and said with tears, "Lady Sun, I have a matter of great urgency in my heart. I shall speak plainly."

Lady Sun said, "What must the lord say may be told."

Liu Bei said, "Your brother and Zhou Yu worked together and first invited you to join Liu Bei not for your sake, but to imprison him and seize Jing Province. Once Jing Province is taken, he surely intends to kill me. So you were bait to draw Liu Bei. I did not come though I feared death, because I believed you, in your man's heart, would pity me. Yesterday I heard that Wu Hou would seek to harm us and that he used the danger in Jing Province to justify our return. Now he sends men behind us to chase and Zhou Yu sends men ahead to block. Only you can untie this danger. If you do not consent, I shall die in the cart to repay your virtue."

Lady Sun cried out in anger: "My brother no longer treats me as true kin, and how can I meet him with any face? I will loosen my own bonds here."

With that she shouted to her attendants to push the carriage forward. She pulled up the screen and, in her own voice, cried to Xu Sheng and Ding Feng: "Do you two seek rebellion?"

Xu Sheng and Ding Feng at once dismounted and dropped their weapons. Bowing on the carriage step, they said, "How dare we rebel? We only hold the order of Chief Commander Zhou and stand here to wait for Liu Bei."

Lady Sun roared in anger: "How dare Zhou Yu, who calls himself treacherous, act this way in my Eastern Wu! Liu Bei is the Great Han uncle, and he is my husband. I told mother and brother that we would return to Jing Province. Why have you, by choosing this place by the mountain path, brought men and horses to block the road and seek to loot my household?"

Xu Sheng and Ding Feng stood and repeatedly nodded, saying, "We do not dare. Put down your anger, Lady. This is none of our concern. It is Zhou the Chief Commander whose order we obey."

Lady Sun snapped, "You fear Zhou Yu, but not me? Zhou Yu can kill you, but if he wrongs me, why should I not kill Zhou Yu?" Then she scolded Zhou Yu in public. She ordered the carriage to move.

Xu Sheng and Ding Feng thought, "We are underlings; how could we withstand her?" and, seeing Zhao Yun in fierce anger, they made the troops hold their breath and opened a wide road for them through.

As soon as they moved only five or six li, Chen Wu and Pan Zhang arrived from behind.

Beforehand, Xu Sheng and Ding Feng had conveyed the whole matter. Chen and Pan said, "You let him through by mistake. We two came at our lord's command to seize him and take him back."

The four commanders assembled the soldiers and rushed on. As Liu Bei walked, behind him a loud cry rose.

Liu Bei said to Lady Sun, "Now the pursuers have reached us again. What should we do?"

Lady Sun said, "Husband, go ahead. I will stand behind with Zi'long."

Liu Bei first drew three hundred troops and moved toward the riverbank. Zi'long reined in at the carriage side, ordered the soldiers to spread out, and prepared to meet the coming cavalry.

When the four commanders arrived and saw Lady Sun, they dismounted and stood with hands clasped.

Lady Sun said, "Chen Wu and Pan Zhang, what business brings you here?"

The two generals answered, "By command of the lord, we bid Lady and Lord Liu return."

Lady Sun spoke in stern voice and said, "It is you and your sort of small men who sowed discord between my brother and me. I have already married another man. Today my return is no elopement. I came with my mother's order and I and my husband must return to Jing Province. Even if my brother himself comes, he must act by ritual propriety. Does one armed with troops have he now intended to kill me?"

She spoke so harshly that the four men glanced at one another and each thought: "For ten thousand years she is no more than sister and brother. Plus Empress Dowager rules now. Wu Hou is a son of devotion. How dare anyone ignore his mother's word? Tomorrow the face may turn, and then it will be said we failed. Better to act as people of feeling." In the ranks they saw no Liu Bei, only Zhao Yun with eyes blazing and brows knit, waiting to fight. So the four commanders repeatedly bowed and withdrew.

Lady Sun told the attendants to move the cart forward.

Xu Sheng said, "We four should go report this to Commander Zhou."

The four hesitated, when suddenly a force came like a whirlwind. It was Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai.

The two commanders asked, "Have any of you seen Liu Bei?"

The four said, "He passed this way earlier. It has already been half a day."

Jiang Qin said, "Why did you not seize him?"

The four each spoke of Lady Sun's rebuke. Jiang Qin said, "Wou Hou fears this very situation and gave this sword to be delivered here: first kill his sister, then behead Liu Bei. Anyone who disobeys will be beheaded."

The four replied, "He is now too far. What can we do?"

Jiang Qin said, "These are only foot soldiers; they cannot catch pace with you. Let Xu Sheng and Ding Feng report to Commander Zhou quickly and order them to row fast boats by water. As for us, we will pursue from the bank. River or land, we will overtake and kill."

So Xu Sheng and Ding Feng rushed to report to Zhou Yu, and Jiang Qin, Zhou Tai, Chen Wu, and Pan Zhang led men along the river and pursued.

Meanwhile Liu Bei and his party, moving fast, went farther from Chaisang, and reached Liu Lang Port. Their hearts were a little at ease. Along the riverbank, they searched for crossing, and there was no boat in sight. Liu Bei and his attendants stood still a while.

Zhao Yun said, "My lord escaped from the tiger's jaws; now we are almost in our own boundary. I know the strategist must have planned this. Why do we still worry?"

Hearing him, Liu Bei suddenly remembered the prosperity in Eastern Wu and could not stop tears.

Later people wrote this poem:

When Wu and Shu were married, the water was clear, pearls spread on the canopy, house of gold in gleam. Who knew one woman, light as heaven under all men, sought to change Liu Lang's steadfast heart.

Liu Bei ordered Zi'long to scout ahead for boats. He reported at once that dust was rising thick from behind.

Liu Bei mounted and looked back from a high place. He saw soldiers and horse covering the ground and said, "Days of running are over; men are tired and horses spent, and the pursuers have arrived again. There is no place to die!"

Then as the shouts came nearer, an auspicious sight appeared on the bank: more than twenty covered boats with drooped awnings were being tossed in a single line on the river.

Zhao Yun said, "By heaven's favor, ships are here! Oar across to the opposite bank and keep distance!"

Liu Bei and Lady Sun hurried onto the boat. Zi'long brought all five hundred troops aboard as well.

Suddenly one in the boat with a silk kerchief and ceremonial robe rose laughingly and said, "My lord, rejoice! Kongming has waited here for a long time." The attendants who appeared to be guests in the boat were all river soldiers from Jing Province.

Liu Bei rejoiced greatly. Soon the four commanders arrived.

Kongming laughed, pointed to the men on shore and said, "I have prepared this for many days. Go and tell Zhou what you have seen, and he should stop using these tricks with beauty."

As they sent arrows from the bank, the boat was far enough.

The four commanders only stared in amazement.

As Liu Bei and Kongming traveled onward, suddenly the river roared hard. Looking back, they saw countless battle ships. Under the battle pennant at the front, Zhou Yu himself led the seasoned river troops, with Huang Gai on his left and Han Dang on his right. Their momentum was like flying horses, their speed like falling stars.

As the chase closed, Kongming ordered the rowers to turn toward the north bank, abandon the boats, and all dismount and continue on foot.

Zhou Yu reached the bank and dismounted to pursue. Everyone else also disembarked and gave chase on foot, except one mounted officer.

Zhou Yu was in front, with Huang Gai, Han Dang, Xu Sheng, and Ding Feng close behind. Zhou Yu asked the soldiers where they were. They said, "The front is the head of Huangzhou Commandery."

Looking ahead and seeing Liu Bei's horsemen not far away, Zhou Yu ordered a massed pursuit.

As they chased, a drum beat resounded. From the valley emerged a line of sword-bearing men, and at its head a leading general.

It was Guan Yu, whose courtesy name was Yunchang.

Zhou Yu lost his composure and spurred his horse to flee. As he fled, Guan Yunchang came on. Zhou Yu leapt forward on horseback and raced for his life. At that moment, on the left rode Huang Zhong, and on the right Wei Yan; both sides surged forward and the Wu armies were smashed.

Zhou Yu climbed into a boat in urgency, but all the infantry soldiers called out together, "Zhou Lang's clever plan to stabilize the realm now costs us the Lady and loss of troops!"

Zhou Yu said in fury, "Let us return and do battle decisively once more!"

Huang Gai and Han Dang held him back by force. Zhou Yu thought to himself, "My scheme has failed. With what face can I go back before Wu Hou?"

He cried out once, a wound in his chest split open, and he sank into the boat. The commanders rushed to save him, but he was already insensible.

It ended with this:

Twice I play at trickery and make it clumsy, today I keep angry words and yet still carry shame. How Commander Zhou's life will continue, we do not yet know.

How this turned out will be told in the next chapter.
chapters.title: Liu Bei Cleverly Angers Lady Sun; Zhuge Liang Unleashes a Second Stratagem Against Zhou Gongjin

chapters.html:
Zhou Yu, whose courtesy name was Gongjin, had been routed in one clash by Zhuge Liang, Kongming, who had laid an ambush for him beforehand with Guan Yu, Huang Zhong, and Wei Yan, each with a column of horsemen. Huang Gai and Han Dang rushed forward to help; they shoved away innumerable boats from the river force. From a hilltop, Liu Bei, whose courtesy name was Xuande, and Lady Sun with her attendants and escorts stopped to watch. How could Zhou Yu not burn with anger? His arrow wound had not yet fully healed. In the surge of rage, the wound split and he fainted to the deck. His officers revived him, then hurriedly boarded and withdrew. Kongming ordered that no pursuit be made, and then returned with Liu Bei to Jing Province to celebrate, rewarding the commanders.

When Zhou Yu came back to Chaisang, Jiang Qin and the rest of the escorting force returned south to Xuxu and reported to Sun Quan. Sun Quan could not contain himself in anger and wanted to appoint Cheng Pu as Chief Commander and raise troops to recover Jing Province. Zhou Yu then submitted another memorial asking for action to repay his grudge. Zhang Zhao remonstrated.

“Do not.” “Cao Cao has thought of this Red Cliffs grievance day and night. He therefore fears Liu and Sun becoming one. That is why he has not yet dared to strike. Now if our lord acts from a momentary fury and swallows each other in haste, Cao Cao will surely march in and pounce. Our state will stand on a knife-edge.”

Gu Yong said, “How, is there not a minor clerk in Xu City for this purpose? If Cao Cao knows that Sun and Liu are not at peace, he will surely stir up Liu Bei against us. Liu Bei, fearing Eastern Wu, will then throw himself beneath Cao Cao. If that happens, when will Jiangnan ever come to peace? For our plans at this moment, best is this: send someone to Xu City, and report that Liu Bei has been appointed Governor of Jing Province. Once Cao Cao hears it, he will fear to send armies southeast. At the same time, make Liu Bei not resent our lord. After that, use my trusted men to spread rumors and split Cao and Liu into mutual conflict. Then we seize the chance. That will serve us best.”

Sun Quan said, “Yong’s words are excellent. But who could be sent?”

“Among us is one man whom Cao Cao admires. He could serve as envoy.” “Who is it?” “Hua Xin is here. Why not send him?”

Sun Quan was delighted and immediately sent him off with a memorial to Xu City. Hua Xin accepted the charge and set out. He traveled straight to Xu City to request audience with Cao Cao. Hearing that Cao Cao was hosting his ministers at Ye County for the Bronze Sparrow festivities, Hua Xin went there and waited on him.

Since Cao Cao’s defeat at Red Cliffs, he had been constantly planning revenge; only suspicion that Sun and Liu were acting in concert had held him from moving quickly. In the spring of the fifteenth year of Jian’an, the Bronze Sparrow Terrace was finished. Cao Cao convened all civil and military officials at Ye County for a great banquet in celebration. The platform stood on the bank of the Zhang River. In the center rose the Bronze Sparrow Terrace; to its left stood the Yulong Terrace, to its right the Jinfeng Terrace, each ten zhang high. Two bridges joined them broadside to side, with a thousand gateways and ten thousand doors. Gold and jade gleamed together.

That day, Cao Cao wore a bejeweled gold crown, a green brocade robe of horsehair silk, a jade belt and pearl-soled shoes, and sat on the height above all. Civil officials and military officers stood below. Desiring to watch the horsemen prove their bowcraft, Cao Cao had a man in a robe of Xichuan crimson silk drape it on a willow branch, fixing an arrow-shooting range and marking the boundary at one hundred paces. The military men were split into two divisions. Cao clan members all wore red, while all other officers and soldiers wore green.

Each man carried a carved bow and a fine arrow, mounted and bridled as if for charge, waiting for command.

Cao Cao issued orders: “Whoever can shoot through the bullseye marked at the center of the target shall receive this brocade robe. Whoever misses shall drink a full cup of water as penalty.”

As soon as he gave the command, from the red-robed line a young general spurred forth. Looking at him, it was Cao Xiu.

He rode back and forth three times, running at speed, nocked an arrow, drew to the ear, and loosed. The shaft flew straight into the red center. The drums and gongs rang together and all shouted in approval. From above on the platform Cao Cao smiled broadly and said, “This is a thousand-li stallion of my own house!”

He moved to have the robe brought to Cao Xiu, when another rider dashed out from the red-robed line, crying, “The Chancellor’s robe is for an outsider to claim first; one should not jostle within the clan!”

Cao Cao saw him: it was Wen Ping.

The officers cried, “Watch Wen Zhongye shoot!”

Wen Ping drew his bow and loosed a single arrow as he urged his horse; he too hit the red center. All cheered, and gongs and drums thundered in disorderly joy.

Wen Ping called loudly, “Bring the robe!”

Again, from the red-robed file another rider sprang out, voice ringing: “Wen Lied shot first. How can you contest this? See how I too split the heart!” He drew to fullness and loosed, striking the center as well.

The eyes of the gathered men turned to him. It was Cao Hong.

He reached for the robe, and from the green line another general surged out.

“Your three-way shooting is no marvel. Watch me shoot!”

It was Zhang He.

Zhang He turned in the saddle and shot backward over his shoulder, also striking the center. Four arrows now clustered in the heart.

Everyone said, “What an archer!”

Zhang He said, “That robe is mine by right!”

He had not finished the words when once again a rider shot forth from the red line, crying, “You call it a feat to turn in the saddle and shoot backward? Watch me take that heart!”

The man was Xiahou Yuan.

He drove forward to the boundary, twisted in place and loosed. His arrow flew among the four that already struck.

The drums and gongs rang as one.

He reined in and shouted over his bow, “Can one steal a robe with this shot?”

From the green side, another rider answered at once, crying, “Set it aside for me—Xu Huang!”

Xiahou Yuan snapped, “Have you any trick other than that to claim my robe?”

Xu Huang replied, “You hitting the red heart is nothing to write home about. Watch me claim the brocade in a single draw.”

He drew, set arrow to string, aimed across the willow pole, loosed—its shaft cut exactly through the willow branch, and the brocade fluttered down. Xu Huang snatched the robe and slung it over his shoulders. He rode to the platform and, with salutes, said, “Thanks to the Chancellor for the robe!”

Cao Cao and all the officers exclaimed with envy. Xu Huang wheeled back to move away, but suddenly at the platform’s edge a green-robed general vaulted out and shouted, “Where are you going with that robe? Put it down and give it to me first!”

They saw Xu Chu.

Xu Huang answered, “The robe is here. Who are you to seize it by force?”

Xu Chu did not answer but came riding to snatch. The two horses met close together. Xu Huang struck at Xu Chu’s bow with his own. Xu Chu put his hand on the bow and dragged Xu Huang off his saddle.

Xu Huang could not hold the bow and leapt from his horse. Xu Chu also dismounted. The two locked in grips and battered each other. Cao Cao hastily ordered men to separate them. The robe had already been torn to shreds.

Cao Cao ordered both men onto the platform.

Xu Huang narrowed his eyes in anger, Xu Chu ground his teeth. Neither would release each other. Cao Cao laughed.

“I merely wished to watch your courage. Who minds one brocade?”

He then ordered all generals up to the platform and gave each a bolt of Shu silk.

Each expressed thanks in turn. Cao Cao then had all return to rank and sit in order. Music blazed forth, with land and river entertainments arranged. Literati and martial officers took turns raising cups and exchanging tribute of wine and toast.

Cao Cao addressed the civil officials.

“The warriors have already shown their valor by horse-and-bow display, and enough is said for military excellence. All of you are men steeped in learning, and now that you have mounted this high terrace, should you not all advance good verses to mark this moment’s triumph?”

All the officials bowed and replied, “We stand ready to obey.”

At that moment, Wang Lang, Zhong Yao, Wang Can, and Chen Lin came forward and presented poems.

Their lines praised Cao Cao’s towering merit and spoke of how rightful it was for him to receive command.

After reading through them all, Cao Cao smiled and said,

“The pieces are fine. You flatter me beyond truth. In my youth I was dull and unworthy and was first selected as a xiaolian candidate, a man of filial piety and incorruptibility. Later, when the realm was in chaos, I built an austere cottage fifty li east of Qiao and meant to spend spring and summer reading and autumn and winter hunting, only to wait for peace under Heaven before entering office. Yet the court called me for recruitment as Commander of the Local Militia, and my intention changed; I wished only to serve the state, bring down bandits, and make merit for it, so that in death I could have a mausoleum inscription reading, ‘The tomb of Cao Hou, General Who Conquers the West of the Former Han.’ That has always been enough for me.

Since dispatching against Dong Zhuo, suppressing the Yellow Turbans, subduing Yuan Shu, defeating Lü Bu, crushing Yuan Shao, and pacifying Liu Biao, I have already brought peace to the realm. To be Chancellor, the honor of a minister at this moment, is the top this state can give. What more is left to seek?

If this land were without my person, who can say how many would call themselves emperor, how many would call themselves king?

Some may see me heavy with power and recklessly infer my heart. They imagine I have strange designs; this is a grave delusion. I have always kept in mind that Confucius praised King Wen of Wen for his self-restraint. Those words pierce me still. What I desire is to relinquish command and troops and accept instead the marquisate of Wuping. Yet that is impossible.

I fear that if I loosened the reins of soldiers and men even once, I would be destroyed by others; if I failed, the realm would totter.

Thus I could never turn from actual danger to idle fame.

No one among you has failed to understand my heart.”

All rose and bowed, saying, “Even Yiyin and Duke Zhou fall short of the Chancellor.”

Later scholars wrote:

Each day Zhou Gong fears a whisper in the street, and Wang Mang bows so humbly to lowly men. Had he fallen by his own hand in that first year, who now would know true and false in all his life?

Cao Cao drank several cups in quick succession and, half intoxicated, summoned an attendant for pen and inkstone and began to write a poem on Bronze Sparrow Terrace. Just as he had touched down the brush, word came in: “A messenger from Eastern Wu named Hua Xin has submitted a memorial recommending that Liu Bei be appointed Governor of Jing Province. Sun Quan has married his sister to Liu Bei; the greater part of the nine commanderies under Heaven now belong to him.”

At the report, Cao Cao’s hands and feet grew unsteady; he tossed the brush aside.

Cheng Yu said, “When your lord stood in ten thousand ranks and faced arrows and stones, he never trembled. Why should you be thus startled now that Liu Bei has obtained Jing Province?”

Cao Cao said, “Liu Bei was a dragon among men and never before has he ever been granted this chance. Now he has obtained Jing Province—it is a trapped dragon entering the sea. How then could I not be moved?”

Cheng Yu said, “Does the Chancellor know the meaning of Hua Xin’s mission?”

Cao Cao said, “I do not.”

Cheng Yu said, “Sun Quan has long mistrusted Liu Bei and wished to raise troops against him, but feared that the Chancellor himself might strike south while he did. Therefore he sent Hua Xin as envoy, recommending Liu Bei. He calms Liu Bei’s heart and fills the Chancellor’s expectations with that.”

Cao Cao nodded. “It is so.”

Cheng Yu said, “I have a plan: let Sun and Liu consume one another, while I seize both by exploiting the opening. One drumbeat can break two enemies.”

Cao Cao delightedly replied, “Your words, Zhongde, match my mind exactly.”

He then summoned Hua Xin back to the platform and bestowed him with additional rewards.

When the banquet dispersed that day, Cao Cao brought officials and officers back to Xuchang and submitted a memorial: appoint Zhou Yu, Gongjin, as Administrator of Nanjun Commandery, and Cheng Pu as Administrator of Jiangxia Commandery. He enfeoffed Hua Xin as Grand Master of the Department of Justice and left him at Xu City.

His order had already reached Eastern Wu, and Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu accepted their posts.

Now that Zhou Yu had taken office at Nanjun, his longing for vengeance grew. He submitted a memorial to his lord, asking that Lu Su be ordered to recapture Jing Province.

Sun Quan told Lu Su,

“Earlier you guarded Jing Province with Liu Bei. He is now delayed in return. When will he move?”

Lu Su said, “The text he gave is clear: once he has obtained Xichuan, he will come back.”

Sun Quan barked, “He only said he would take Xichuan, and yet until now he has still not moved troops. He has made old men wait.”

Lu Su said, “If you permit, I will go and speak.”

He then rode to Jing Province.

Returning to Liu Bei and Kongming, they had gathered grain and trained men in Jing Province. Men of the nearby and distant lands rallied to him. Then came report that Lu Su had arrived.

Liu Bei asked Kongming, “What is Zijing here for?”

Kongming said, “Yesterday Sun Quan petitioned the state to make you Governor of Jing Province, clearly because he fears Cao Cao. Cao Cao now enfeoffed Zhou Yu as Administrator of Nanjun; this is his design to set our two houses against each other, so that he may work from the center. Now Lu Su’s coming means Zhou Yu, already an administrator, comes to demand Jing Province.”

Liu Bei asked, “How shall we answer?”

Kongming said, “If Lu Su raises the matter, let our lord cry aloud in grief. Cry until your pain is piercing; then I will come forth and persuade.”

The arrangement was settled. They received Lu Su at the government hall, exchanged ceremony, and took their seats.

Lu Su said, “Today my lord, the Lord of Wu, has made your marriage to the eastern queen. I, Lu Su, should be your host—how can I sit now?”

Liu Bei laughed.

“This is no matter with me and Zhongjing being old friends. Why this excess of courtesy?”

Lu Su then sat.

After tea, he said, “I come by my lord Wu’s command, solely on the matter of Jing Province. Your Highness has occupied it for some time and has not yet returned it. Now that our two families are bound by marriage, on the basis of kinship alone it should be handed over.”

Hearing this, Liu Bei covered his face and wept.

Lu Su was startled. “Why does the Lord of Xuanda weep so?”

His crying did not cease.

Kongming came out from behind the screen.

“I have heard this long enough. Does Zijing know why my lord weeps?”

Lu Su said, “I truly do not.”

Kongming said, “What is difficult to see? When first my lord received leave in Jing Province, he promised to return it once he obtained Xichuan. Look carefully: in Yi Province, Liu Zhang is our lord’s younger brother’s age, and by kinship all of Han are of one family. If he raises troops to seize that city, outsiders will spit at him. If he does not, then he cannot return Jing and where will he stand? If he returns it now, he loses face before his honorific father-in-law. It is truly a twofold hardship that brings tears from our hearts.”

When Kongming finished, Liu Bei struck his breast and feet against the floor and wept loudly. Lu Su advised,

“Your Highness, do not be so distressed. Discuss this at length with Kongming.”

Kongming said, “I beg you, Zijing, return to Wu and report this burdening matter fully to the Lord. Ask him to allow time, and say our pain is real.”

Lu Su asked, “If your lord does not agree, what then?”

Kongming said, “Since my lord has already married your lord’s younger sister, how can he refuse?”

Lu Su said, “Please speak well and carry this plea back and report again.”

Lu Su was known as a broad-hearted elder. Seeing how Liu Bei grieved, he could only agree. Liu Bei and Kongming thanked him. The banquet ended; they escorted him to his ship and he departed.

He went straight back to Chaisang and told Zhou Yu all this in full. Zhou Yu stamped and said,

“Zijing has again fallen into Kongming’s scheme. When Liu Bei depended on Liu Biao, there was already intent to swallow him. How much more so with Liu Zhang in Xichuan? As this is arranged, your honorable self should not be too secure, old brother.”

“I have a way so that Kongming cannot move within my calculations. Let him follow through.”

Lu Su said, “I wish to hear your clever plan.”

Yohu said, “Zijing need not go back to Wu with this. Go again to Jing Province and tell Liu Bei this: since Sun and Liu are now joined by kinship, the two are one house. If Liu’s men cannot bear to take Xichuan, then Eastern Wu will raise armies and seize it. When we have obtained Xichuan, we will use it as marriage tribute, and in exchange Jing Province will be returned.”

Lu Su said, “Xichuan is far and difficult to take. Can this plan hold?”

Zhou Yu laughed. “You truly are generous of heart, elder. You think I will truly go for Xichuan and seize it for him? I only use the name as pretense. My intent is to take Jing Province, and to make him unready. When Eastern Wu troops and horses pass through Jing on the Sichuan road, I will ask him to provide silver and grain. Liu Bei will surely come out of the city to inspect and reward the soldiers. Then, seizing the moment, we strike and take Jing Province, settle our old grievance, and relieve your threat.”

Lu Su rejoiced and returned again to Jing Province.

Liu Bei and Kongming conferred.

Kongming said, “Lu Su has not truly seen Wu’s lord; he only discussed this with Zhou Yu here at Chaisang. He has come to tempt us. All you need do is nod and answer yes to every word he speaks.”

The plan was set.

When Lu Su entered, ceremony complete, he said, “The Lord of Wu greatly admires Your Highness’s virtue. He and our commanders have discussed taking up arms to retrieve Xichuan for you. Once we take Xichuan, we will exchange it back for Jing Province and use Xichuan as the dowry token. But as the horse and men pass through, he asks for some grain and silver.”

Kongming nodded quickly.

“Such benevolence from the Lord of Wu is hard to find.”

Liu Bei clasped his hands and gave thanks. “It is all Zijing’s words well spoken.”

Kongming said, “When the mighty host arrives, I shall prepare to meet them and honor the troops.”

Lu Su was inwardly delighted. After the banquet he took leave.

Liu Bei asked Kongming, “What does this mean?”

Kongming laughed broadly.

“Zhou Yu’s life is near the end! Even a boy would not be deceived by such a scheme.”

Liu Bei asked, “How?”

Kongming said, “This is the stratagem known as Jia-tu Mie-Guo: a false route to claim Guo. The name is to fetch Sichuan; the intent is to seize Jing. When Your Highness comes out of the city to reward your troops, strike at that unprepared moment and break through. It is all done by surprise.”

Liu Bei said, “How should I proceed?”

Kongming said, “Keep broad and calm. Spend your strength preparing bows for the tiger, and set baiting fragrance to catch the crocodile. Once Zhou Yu arrives, if he survives he will be with nine parts of no breath left.”

Then he called Zhao Yun and added, “Do it in this way; the rest I will set in place.”

Liu Bei rejoiced.

Later poets later sighed:

Zhou Yu devises the plan to take Jing, yet Kongming reads first among all the counsels. He trusted the river’s fragrant bait to hold, not knowing a hook was cast in secret waters.

Returning, Lu Su told Zhou Yu that Liu Bei and Kongming seemed delighted and had no suspicion, preparing to come out and reward their troops.

Zhou Yu laughed. “So this round, we have trapped him too!”

He ordered Lu Su to report back to his lord and sent Cheng Pu with troops in support.

By now Zhou Yu’s arrow wound had mostly healed and his body was sound. He sent Gan Ning in the vanguard, followed by Xu Sheng and Ding Feng, with Ling Tong and Lü Meng as rear guard. Fifty thousand troops by water and land advanced toward Jing Province.

Zhou Yu sat in his boat and often laughed, certain that Kongming had fallen into the snare.

When the vanguard reached Xiakou, Zhou Yu asked,

“Are there men ahead from Jing meeting us?”

They reported, “General Mi Zhu has come to see the Chief Commander.”

Zhou Yu called him in.

“How goes the inspection of troops?” he asked.

Mi Zhu said, “My lord has made all arrangements.”

Zhou Yu said, “Where is the Imperial Uncle?”

Mi Zhu said, “He is at the gate of Jing, waiting. He means to drink with the Commander.”

Zhou Yu said, “Today is for your household’s matters and for campaigning far away. The rites of reward are not to be done lightly.”

Mi Zhu took these words and returned.
